Senses.PreferredTarget: every day is a good day
AlternateTargets: day after day is a good day
Senses.Explanation: Literally, "every day is a good day." Yunmen tells the assembly, "I do not ask you about before the fifteenth day; bring me a phrase about after the fifteenth." When the assembly gives no answer, he answers for them: "every day is a good day." The corpus thereafter quotes it as Yunmen's answer, pairs it with "every year is a good year," challenges it in questions, rebukes a monk who offers it, and expands it in later teaching-seat verse. Its specifically Chan deployment is therefore as Yunmen's public answer and a line later masters openly quote, test, contradict, and comment on; the record supplies no mystical paraphrase for "good."
Senses.Note: 192 occurrences in 100 allowlisted texts. The calendar phrase and Yunmen quotation name the same statement, not separate readings or things.

Occurrences.Kwic: 十五日已前不問汝，十五日已後道將一句來。眾無對。自代曰：日日是好日。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)), in the explicitly headed Yunmen Wenyan section: Yunmen Wenyan asks for a line after the fifteenth day and, when the assembly gives no answer, supplies his own exact answer, ‘Every day is a good day.’

Occurrences.Kwic: 日日是好日，佛法世法盡周畢。不須特地覓幽玄，祇管鉢盂兩度濕。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷): complete-case exact-turn review identifies Miaozong as the actor for this occurrence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 年年是好年，日日是好日。師云：瞎老婆吹火。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chushi Fanqi (楚石梵琦禪師語錄), Chushi Fanqi's New Year's Eve informal convocation. An unnamed monk is the exact speaker who advances 'every year is a good year; every day is a good day'; Chushi answers, 'a blind old woman blows the fire.' The line, expanded context, section header, book title, TEI header, exact-case search, and independent parallel witnesses preserve the exchange without naming this monk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 日日是好日年年是好年為甚𨚫無師曰張公喫酒李公醉
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Connected Anthology of Verses on Old Chan Cases (禪宗頌古聯珠通集): an unnamed monk tells Mingjiao Kuan that every day is a good day and every year a good year, then asks why there is no New Year Buddha-dharma. The line, expanded context, section header, book title, TEI header, and parallel-passage search do not give a personal name for the unnamed monk.
